I farm only 2 mu, so I count every bag. I do not like taking big risks. What I usually do is start from what worked last year, then look at the fields around me. Here in Quzhou, with well water, if wheat and maize want good yield, I will not cut fertilizer too hard. If I save a little on fertilizer and lose yield, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. Since I have done this for many years, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on the full 2 mu. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put the main fertilizer in first, water about 3 times if the season is normal, and spray 2 times if I see weeds or disease pressure. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed, because that has worked better around here for years, then I will topdress nitrogen after it gets going, water 2 times with well irrigation if rain is not enough, and spray about 2 times for weeds and insects. I will use rotary tillage because my land is small and this is the easiest and most common way for me to manage it.
